paper.title_en: The elliptic wind on jet wakes in high-energy heavy-ion collisions
paper.abstract_en: Energy loss by fast partons induces Mach-cone-like medium response as they propagate inside the hot quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Since the hot QGP is nonuniform whose initial density gradient also generates collective flow, jet-induced medium response in this dynamic system should also be distorted by the flow and density gradient. The distortion is shown to lead to a broadened jet wake whose transverse width depends on the azimuthal angle of the jet propagation due to the elliptic anisotropy of the density gradient and the flow velocity in non-central heavy-ion collisions. We propose and calculate the in-plane and out-plane differences of the azimuthal-dependent jet-hadron correlations for soft charged hadrons in $γ$-jet events as measures of the elliptic broadening of the wake front and deepening of the diffusion wake. We also study the sensitivity of this observable to the shear viscosity of the QGP medium. Experimental measurements of the azimuthal modulation of the jet wake due to the wind of the elliptic flow at RHIC and LHC can provide further constraints on the transport properties of the QGP medium.
